articles.title: Two-time boxing champion Zolani Tete dead at the age of 38 following a terrifying balaclava-clad ambush
articles.standfirst: The boxer was arriving at his residence when he was ambushed by two armed suspects
articles.summary: The boxer was arriving at his residence when he was ambushed by two armed suspects
articles.body:
Former world boxing champion Zolani Tete was killed in a shooting outside his home in South Africa , government officials reported.

Thus, the country's Minister of Sports, Gayton McKenzie, said that Tete, 38, died after being shot in his car, while a 27-year-old woman who was traveling with him in the vehicle is hospitalized after being shot several times.

Tete, who held WBF flyweight world titles between 2007 and 2008 and the WBO bantamweight title in 2017 and 2019 , was waiting for the door to his home to be opened when he was ambushed by two armed suspects.

"The World Boxing Council (WBC) mourned the passing of Zolani Tete. "Our deepest condolences go out to his family, loved ones, and all those who were touched by his extraordinary career," it said on social media.'

According to some local media, Tete was planning to return to the ring in November after serving a four-year ban for doping. The boxer held the record for the fastest "knockout" in a world title fight by defeating fellow South African Gonya 11 seconds into the opening round in the WBO bantamweight world championship.

articles.title: Oscar de la Hoya’s ex-wife walks away with $13.5M property fortune
articles.standfirst: The former boxer and Millie Corretjer finalized their divorce settlement in 2025
articles.summary: The former boxer and Millie Corretjer finalized their divorce settlement in 2025
articles.body:
Oscar De La Hoya's divorce settlement has resulted in a substantial real estate transfer, with his former wife, M ilagros “Millie” Corretjer, receiving full ownership of two properties in Puerto Rico valued at a combined $13.5 million.

According to court documents obtained by TMZ, Corretjer was awarded both properties as part of the former couple's confidential divorce judgment. The latest filing does not alter the terms of their settlement but formally clears the way for the properties to be transferred into Corretjer's name.

The two properties include a residence in San Juan assigned a value of $3.5 million and another property at the Bahia Beach Resort in Rio Grande valued at $10 million. Under the agreement, both properties became Corretjer's sole and separate property, meaning De La Hoya has no remaining claim to either one.

Why the properties were awarded to Millie Corretjer

The court filing was necessary because Puerto Rico requires a certified court order to complete the transfer of real estate following a divorce. The documents therefore provide additional clarity about one part of a settlement whose broader financial terms remain private. De La Hoya and Corretjer finalized their divorce settlement in 2025, ending a marriage that had lasted more than two decades.

Although the couple had been separated for years, their legal divorce process took considerably longer to complete. The $13.5 million in Puerto Rico real estate represents one of the few publicly disclosed elements of their confidential agreement.

A marriage that was always under the spotlight

De la Hoya and Corretjer first met in 2000 and married in October 2001. The couple went on to have three children together: one son and two daughters. Their relationship eventually came to an end, however. The couple separated in 2016, and De la Hoya did not formally file for divorce until January 2023.

The divorce was ultimately settled in 2025, with the remaining terms kept confidential. The latest court filing essentially handles the administrative work necessary to implement the real estate portion of that agreement. The properties awarded to Corretjer add another dimension to the enormous wealth accumulated by De la Hoya during and after his legendary boxing career.

The Mexican American fighter became one of the most recognizable boxers of his generation, winning world titles in six weight classes and earning the nickname “The Golden Boy.” De la Hoya retired from boxing in 2009 with a professional record of 39-6 and 30 knockouts.

His career inside the ring was followed by an equally significant role as a promoter through Golden Boy Promotions, which he founded in 2002. That business helped De la Hoya remain one of the most influential figures in boxing long after his own fighting career ended.

articles.title: Canelo won’t rule out a historic bout at Mexico’s most iconic stadium
articles.standfirst: The proposal generated excitement among boxing fans all over the world
articles.summary: The proposal generated excitement among boxing fans all over the world
articles.body:
S aúl “Canelo” Álvarez has fought in some of the most iconic venues in boxing, from sold-out arenas in Las Vega s to packed stadiums across the globe. Yet one stage remains absent from his remarkable résumé: Mexico City's legendary Estadio Azteca, but t hat could eventually change.

The undisputed Mexican superstar recently revealed that he is open to the possibility of fighting at Estadio Azteca after receiving a public invitation from Emilio Azcárraga, chairman of Televisa and one of the key figures behind the stadium's future plans.

For a fighter who has spent more than a decade carrying the sport's biggest events, the idea of stepping into the ring at one of Mexico's most historic sporting venues appears to hold special significance.

An invitation from one of Mexico's most influential figures

The possibility emerged when Azcárraga discussed his vision for Estadio Azteca following its ongoing modernization efforts. As part of a broader plan to reestablish the venue as a destination for major sporting events, Azcárraga floated the idea of hosting a future Canelo fight at the stadium. He pointed to the rich boxing history associated with the venue and suggested that Álvarez could help usher in a new era for the iconic facility.

The proposal generated excitement among boxing fans. Estadio Azteca has long been considered one of the most important sports venues in the world. Known as the " Colossus of Santa Úrsula," the stadium has hosted World Cup finals, historic soccer matches, and some of the most memorable moments in Mexican sports history. Adding a Canelo Álvarez fight to that list would create another landmark event.

Speaking with TUDN, Álvarez did not dismiss the possibility. Instead, he welcomed it. "For me, it would be an honor, and I'm not ruling it out at all. I hope that one day I get the chance to fight there," Álvarez said. The comments represent the strongest indication yet that boxing's biggest Mexican star would seriously consider bringing one of his future bouts to the famed stadium.

Álvarez also emphasized the unique atmosphere that Estadio Azteca creates, acknowledging the emotional connection millions of Mexican sports fans have with the venue. While no fight has been scheduled and no negotiations have been announced, the fact that Canelo openly embraced the concept has already fueled speculation about what such an event could look like.

A potential career-defining farewell

The idea carries significance beyond a single fight. At 36 years old and already a future Hall of Famer, Álvarez has entered the latter stages of a career that has transformed him into one of the most accomplished fighters in boxing history. A bout at Estadio Azteca could serve as more than just another title defense or pay-per-view attraction. It could become a celebration of his legacy.

For years, many of Canelo's biggest fights have taken place in the United States, where he developed into one of boxing's premier attractions. Returning to Mexico for a major stadium event would give his home-country supporters a rare opportunity to witness one of the sport's biggest stars in an unforgettable setting.

articles.title: Katie Taylor wins her farewell fight in front of 80,000 people
articles.standfirst: One of the greatest female boxers of all time retires at the age of 40 with 26 victories and a single defeat
articles.summary: One of the greatest female boxers of all time retires at the age of 40 with 26 victories and a single defeat
articles.body:
Katie Taylor brought her extraordinary career to an end with a resounding victory over the Frenchwoman Flora Pili, who until yesterday had been unbeaten, in front of 80,000 fans at Croke Park (Dublin) . The Irishwoman, who won Olympic gold when women’s boxing made its debut at London 2012, fulfilled her final wish: to fight in Ireland’s sporting cathedral.

Taylor, 40, dominated her opponent over 10 rounds, earning a unanimous decision victory and retiring as the undisputed 140-pound champion (63.503 kg).

Taylor (26-1) added the vacant WBC super lightweight title to her WBO, WBA, and IBF belts . The judges’ scores were 100-90, 100-90, and 98-91. Pili’s record is 12-1 with this defeat.

" In April 2022, Taylor defeated Amanda Serrano in a packed Madison Square Garden , in what was the first women's boxing match to headline the venue. The two have faced each other three times in total, with Taylor victorious on every occasion, most recently in 2025. That trilogy is the most iconic part of her incredible career.

This latest victory capped an extraordinary journey for Taylor, who began boxing at a time when girls were forbidden from competing as amateurs in Ireland and sometimes took part in bouts simply as "K Taylor".

“Croke Park! We did it! The people of Ireland gave me a dream ending to a dream career. Nothing can top this. Without a doubt, this was the crowning moment of my entire career”

The Irishwoman, who made her professional debut in 2016, retires with 26 victories (6 by KO) and only one defeat , the one suffered against American Chantelle Cameron when moving up to the super lightweight division after having widely dominated the lightweight division.

That happened on May 20, 2023 and just half a year later and at the same venue, Dublin's 3Arena, Taylor got her full revenge.

From the Olympic dream to the dream retirement

After the fight, the Irishwoman placed her gloves in the center of the ring to symbolize her retirement , while her team helped place the belts around them.

After the fight, addressing the euphoric crowd, she said: “Croke Park! We did it! The people of Ireland gave me a dream ending to a dream career. Nothing can top this. Without a doubt, this was the crowning moment of my entire career”.

“ I began my career with the dream of becoming an Olympic champion . I achieved it, but these last 10 years have exceeded my most optimistic expectations. They have been 10 extraordinary years,” Taylor concluded.

articles.body:
Next Saturday, September 12, the world of boxing will experience a historic night that promises plenty of excitement when the World Boxing Council (WBC) welterweight world champion, Ryan Garcia , defends his belt for the first time against the dangerous British contender Conor Benn , at the T-Mobile Arena in Las Vegas, Nevada.

"García arrives as champion after capturing the WBC welterweight title against Mario Barrios , while Benn will face the biggest opportunity of his career, trying to become a world champion for the first time. Both fighters want to secure the victory to establish themselves in the elite of international boxing.

García will rely on his speed and endurance to retain his world welterweight champion title, while his opponent, a fighter of British origin who is also the son of legendary world champion Nigel Benn , seeks to write his own chapter in the family's boxing history.

Therefore, at MARCA MX we will tell you what the prediction is and everything you need to know about the Ryan Garcia vs Conor Benn fight.

What is the prediction for the Ryan Garcia vs Conor Benn fight?

Experts and analysts pointed out that this fight will be highly competitive because Benn can make things difficult for any opponent due to his aggressiveness, physical strength, and offensive mindset.

For his part, García has skills such as speed, precision, and counterpunching power to make the difference in this fight, so the current champion is the favorite to win this bout.

articles.title: Canelo Álvarez on Julio César Chávez's feat: “Mexico deserves it, it is the right time”
articles.standfirst: The head of the Council expects an attractive fight card in the country
articles.summary: The head of the Council expects an attractive fight card in the country
articles.body:
A few weeks ago Emilio Azcárraga spoke about the possibility of a Canelo Álvarez fight at the Estadio Azteca , just as happened with Julio César Chávez in 1993 with nearly 133,000 fans in attendance for his victory over Greg Haugen .

For Mauricio Sulaimán , the president of the World Boxing Council , in Mexico it is a good time for an event of that magnitude to take place, due to the passion there is in Mexico for boxing and sports in general, he spoke in EXCLUSIVE for MARCA MX .

Sulaimán, WBC president: “We will always have champions and quality”

Sulaimán, present at the premiere of the new documentary about Julio César Chávez , which premieres on Vix next Friday, September 11, spoke about the quality of Mexican boxing.

“We have William Zepeda , who has just won a world title, Camarón Zepeda, Divino Espinosa . There is a great amount of talent in national boxing, both men and women, and we will always be one of the countries with the greatest number of champions, but above all quality.”

“The boxing serves a great role in society. Both in Mexico and in all countries, every boxer in a gym is a person off the streets where one finds easy ways out for many things, where one can find a wrong path in life,” said the head of the WBC .

Does Canelo Álvarez to the Azteca Stadium?

A few weeks ago Azcárraga said that “ there is an opportunity, for example, I would make a call to Canelo . It would be worth doing one of the fights Canelo has.”

For his part, Saúl Álvarez added that he likes the idea: “it is always an honor to fight in Mexico and in front of my people, even more so in a stadium like the Estadio Azteca , which we all know.”

Sulaimán thinks it is a good time for an event to take place at what is now the Banorte Stadium , but it is not the only historic venue.

“It is necessary, Mexico deserves it, the Mexican fans deserve it. We have, as I was saying, a large number of boxers and above all, being able to have an event, a sellout at the Azteca for Canelo would be wonderful, a carnival of championships at the Plaza de Toros . There have been a great number of highly important fights in our country and I feel that this is the right moment .”

articles.title: How much money does the winner of Ryan Garcia vs Conor Benn take home? This is the multimillion-dollar purse for the fight

articles.summary: This fight is for the WBC Welterweight World Championship
articles.body:
The World Boxing Council (WBC) will put the welterweight championship held by Ryan García on the line next Saturday, September 12, against the dangerous Conor Benn in Las Vegas, Nevada, United States. This matchup has sparked a lot of interest among the followers of both pugilists to find out what will happen in the future of the division.

In addition, both boxers' records as professionals are very similar, which suggests it will be a great fight that could go to the judges' decision, since both have amassed 25 victories as professionals, while in defeats Ryan García has two and Conor Benn only one, but now the question is how many millions each fighter will take home in this battle for the WBC Welterweight World Championship.

How much money does the winner of Ryan Garcia vs Conor Benn take home?

Ryan Garcia and Conor Benn face off in one of the most compelling bouts in international boxing, with major sporting and financial interests at stake. The fight not only pits two of the division’s most high-profile figures against each other, but also generates substantial revenue through broadcasting on DAZN , PPV sales, and the box office at the T-Mobile Arena in Las Vegas , where ticket sales surpassed $6.3 million on the first day.

As for how much money the winner takes home, there is no official and public figure earmarked exclusively for whoever prevails in the fight. The final amount will depend on the guaranteed purses that Garcia and Benn have negotiated, in addition to their possible shares of the PPV revenue and the gate.

However, various industry reports and rumors have cited guaranteed purses of around $15 million or more for fighters at this level, although these amounts have not been officially confirmed for this bout. articles.standfirst: Two controversial stars collide in Las Vegas with a world title and redemption on the line
articles.summary: Two controversial stars collide in Las Vegas with a world title and redemption on the line
articles.body:
Las Vegas has seen plenty of unlikely boxing attractions, but Ryan Garcia and Conor Benn arriving together at T-Mobile Arena may be one of the most combustible yet.

The WBC welterweight championship is on the line, while both fighters are carrying reputations that have made them as fascinating outside the ring as inside it.

Garcia , America’s social-media superstar, has the belt and the greater profile. Benn has the famous surname, a relentless work ethic and something perhaps even more valuable: the determination to silence his doubters. Officially, Garcia enters at 25-2 with 20 knockouts, while Benn is 25-1 with 14 stoppages.

Their records tell only part of the story. Both men have endured damaging controversies involving banned substances. Benn’s career was derailed after two positive tests for clomifene emerged in 2022, while Garcia served a year-long suspension after testing positive for ostarine following his 2024 victory over Devin Haney.

Now those turbulent chapters have been followed by one of boxing’s biggest commercial opportunities. Reports have placed the combined purse at roughly $30 million, potentially giving each fighter an eight-figure payday.

The reported reward is another indication of how far Benn’s marketability has carried him despite the controversy surrounding his career.

The Briton has also been driven by something more personal. He wants to follow in the footsteps of his father, Nigel Benn, and capture the WBC title that once helped define the elder Benn’s legacy.

A victory would give Conor his first world championship and provide another chapter in one of British boxing’s most recognizable family stories.

A fight where pressure cuts both ways

The physical challenge may be just as significant as the psychological one for Benn . He hasn’t competed at the 147-pound welterweight limit for several years and has recently operated at much heavier weights.

Cutting back down has been an exhausting process, but Benn made the championship limit, declaring that discipline had carried him through what he described as an exceptionally difficult camp.

Garcia , meanwhile, believes that weight reduction could become a major factor once the action begins. The American has questioned whether Benn’s body will recover quickly enough from the demanding cut, suggesting that his opponent could be more vulnerable to punches as the fight progresses.

Garcia has his own pressure to handle. He’s making the first defense of the WBC championship he won against Mario Barrios , and another disappointing performance would create more questions around a career that has repeatedly shifted between spectacular performances and serious controversy.

That unpredictability is what makes this matchup so compelling. Garcia possesses explosive speed, accuracy and natural athleticism, while Benn brings aggression, durability and an unwillingness to back away from difficult exchanges. Neither fighter appears interested in a cautious opening.

There’s also plenty of psychological warfare as Garcia expects Benn to come forward aggressively, while Benn has promised to bring ferocity and intensity from the opening bell.

The money will be enormous, the championship priceless and the spotlight unforgiving, but beyond the reported $30 million payday, Saturday’s fight offers both men the chance for control over the next chapter of their careers.

For the first time, the American-Mexican boxer, Ryan García will headline the boxing card for Mexico’s Independence Day celebrations this Saturday, September 12 at the T-Mobile Arena in Las Vegas, Nevada, and his debut will have a special setting as he will make the first defense of his World Boxing Council welterweight title against British fighter C onor Benn . It is worth remembering that the Californian won the title in February 2026 by defeating Mario Barrios.

"King Ryan" is looking to rebuild his career after a period in which he faced a mental health crisis , tested positive in a doping control, and received a suspension that kept him out of the ring for one year after testing positive for ostarine , a banned performance-enhancing substance, in tests related to his fight against Devin Haney on April 20, 2024. Since that period, he has worked to reposition himself among boxing’s top attractions and further away from stories outside the ring . His effort is paying off, and he will headline this weekend’s Patria Card along with 8 other fights.

What are the fights on the Ryan Garcia vs Ben Connor card?

Without a doubt, the most attractive fight of the night is the one starring Ryan Garcia, who will arrive with a record of 25 victories (20 by way of KO) and 2 defeats. However, Conor Benn will have his first fight as a challenger for a world title belt, and he comes off defeating Regis Prograis by unanimous decision at Tottenham Hotspur Stadium in London. The son of former international monarch Nigel Benn arrives with credentials of 25 wins (14 KOs) and just one defeat, but also with the desire to end his knockout drought, having not finished a fight by this route for four years.

Another fight that has drawn attention is that of Australian Jai Opetaia against Lithuanian Noel Mikaelian , billed as a power war in the cruiserweight division . articles.title: Fernando Vargas, boxing legend, in spotlight after son arrested following Universal Studios car crash
articles.standfirst: Fernando Vargas Jr. was taken into custody on suspicion of DUI after a three-vehicle collision in California.
articles.summary: Fernando Vargas Jr. was taken into custody on suspicion of DUI after a three-vehicle collision in California.
articles.body:
Former world champion Fernando Vargas has found his family back in the headlines after his son, Fernando Vargas Jr ., was arrested following a car crash at Universal Studios.

The incident happened Thursday night in a Universal Studios parking structure, where the younger Vargas was involved in a three-vehicle collision shortly before 8 p.m.

"Boxer Fernando Vargas Jr. was arrested Thursday night following a three-vehicle crash in a Universal Studios parking structure," an NBC 4 report cited by EssentiallySports stated.

Authorities said nobody was injured in the collision, but Vargas Jr . was taken into custody on suspicion of driving under the influence of alcohol.

Fernando Vargas Jr. arrested on suspicion of DUI

"The California Highway Patrol said in a news release that Vargas Jr. was arrested on suspicion of driving under the influence of alcohol in the crash reported just before 8 p.m. No injuries were reported in connection with the crash. The CHP will present the case to county prosecutors for consideration of charges."

The case has not yet resulted in a confirmed conviction, and prosecutors will now decide whether formal charges should be brought.

A short video reportedly recorded before the crash also surfaced afterward, showing Vargas Jr . shirtless alongside an unidentified woman. The circumstances surrounding the collision itself remain unclear.

Another controversy for Fernando Vargas Jr.

The arrest comes months after Vargas Jr . was involved in another incident that drew attention away from his boxing career.

Earlier in 2026, footage circulated showing him in an altercation with his younger brother Amado Vargas inside a Las Vegas hotel lobby. Reports at the time suggested personal issues may have been behind the confrontation.

Vargas Jr . has been a professional boxer since 2020 and gained greater attention after facing Callum Walsh on the undercard of the Terence Crawford and Canelo Alvarez event. He lost that light middleweight contest by unanimous decision.

He later switched to bare-knuckle boxing and returned in London on July 25, defeating Allen Gary Jhon by second-round knockout at BKB 57.

His father, Fernando Vargas , remains one of the better-known names of his generation after becoming a world champion during his own career.

Now, however, the Vargas family is attracting attention for events outside the ring, with the younger Vargas waiting to learn whether prosecutors will pursue charges following the Universal Studios crash.

articles.standfirst: Mexican boxer Julio César Chávez Jr. crushed Colombian Jeison Troncoso with a devastating knockout in the first round of the fight in Puebla
articles.summary: Mexican boxer Julio César Chávez Jr. crushed Colombian Jeison Troncoso with a devastating knockout in the first round of the fight in Puebla
articles.body:
'As part of a well-attended boxing event , on the night of Saturday, September 12, 2026, the Miguel Hidalgo Gymnasium in the city of Puebla , Mexico, witnessed a dazzling finish inside the ring. Mexican boxer Julio César Chávez Jr. faced off against the experienced Colombian Jeison Troncoso in a bout scheduled within the heavyweight/super middleweight division, where expectations centered on the former world champion's performance . The outcome did not take long to arrive: the "Son of the Legend" needed just 2 minutes and 59 seconds to knock out his opponent before the sound of the first bell , answering the "who, what, when, where, and why" of a fight designed to reaffirm his standing among the elite of professional boxing.'

'From the referee's opening command, Chávez Jr. took the initiative in the ring by backing his rival into a corner with constant punishment to the midsection and combinations to the face. Troncoso tried to keep his distance and protect himself behind a high guard, but the pressure applied by the Mexican quickly wore down his defensive abilities. After landing a lethal left hook that made the South American fighter stagger against the ropes, the Sinaloa native stepped on the gas until he landed a power combination that sent the visiting boxer to the canvas for good .'

The main referee declared the official technical knockout in the final second of the opening round after determining that Troncoso was unable to continue . According to chronicles and reports issued by specialized media outlets such as Récord, Mediotiempo and Tribuna Noticias, the Aztec fighter made it clear from the opening moments that he was looking to end the bout quickly to send a forceful message about his aspirations .

'A renewed boost for the "Son of the Legend"'

With this devastating performance on Puebla soil, Julio César Chávez Jr. extended his good run by earning his third consecutive victory in the professional circuit . This statistic takes on particular relevance because it is a string of wins that the boxer had not been able to put together since the period between 2010 and 2012 , the era before losing his undefeated record and world title to Argentina’s Sergio "Maravilla" Martínez.

The victory allows the boxer to reach the mark of 56 wins in his professional record , 36 of which have come before the limit. As cited by the sports newspaper Récord, the motivation of the son of the great Aztec boxing legend remains intact under the phrase "old are the hills" , expressed in the days beforehand to dismiss questions about his veteran status and his competitive ability .

Debates in the boxing world about the opponent

Despite the resounding result celebrated by the home fans, various sports analysts were quick to scrutinize the demands of the matchup . Media outlets such as Mediotiempo pointed out in their coverage that the level of resistance offered by Jeison Troncoso was noticeably below what was expected , characterizing him as an opponent with limited defensive resources that made the Mexican’s quick finish easier .

However, in Chávez Jr.'s camp, there is satisfaction in maintaining the fighting rhythm and effectiveness in power punches . Sources close to the Sinaloan's camp reaffirm that each appearance in the ring is part of a calculated strategy to gain experience, regain confidence, and climb steps toward a fight with greater media significance.

Fixed goal on a new title opportunity

The emphatic knockout achieved in Puebla consolidates the work plan set by the corner of the Aztec boxer for the second half of his career. After going through difficult years away from the major international spotlight, the consistency shown in his recent appearances opens the door to arranging fights against world-ranked contenders .

"Chávez Jr. has made it clear in repeated statements gathered by coverage from Récord and Tribuna Noticias that his ultimate goal remains to fight again for a major title from the organization that grants the opportunity . The emphatic performance against Jeison Troncoso serves as the necessary calling card to continue on the region's marquee cards .

The main referee declared the official technical knockout in the final second of the opening round after determining that Troncoso was unable to continue . According to chronicles and reports issued by specialized media outlets such as Récord, Mediotiempo and Tribuna Noticias, the Aztec fighter made it clear from the opening moments that he was looking to end the bout quickly to send a forceful message about his aspirations .

With this devastating performance on Puebla soil, Julio César Chávez Jr. extended his good run by earning his third consecutive victory in the professional circuit . Despite the resounding result celebrated by the home fans, various sports analysts were quick to scrutinize the demands of the matchup . Media outlets such as Mediotiempo pointed out in their coverage that the level of resistance offered by Jeison Troncoso was noticeably below what was expected , characterizing him as an opponent with limited defensive resources that made the Mexican’s quick finish easier .

However, in Chávez Jr.'s camp, there is satisfaction in maintaining the fighting rhythm and effectiveness in power punches . Sources close to the Sinaloan's camp reaffirm that each appearance in the ring is part of a calculated strategy to gain experience, regain confidence, and climb steps toward a fight with greater media significance.
Fixed goal on a new title opportunity

The emphatic knockout achieved in Puebla consolidates the work plan set by the corner of the Aztec boxer for the second half of his career. The emphatic performance against Jeison Troncoso serves as the necessary calling card to continue on the region's marquee cards .

articles.body:
Ryan Garcia had just destroyed Conor Benn in two rounds, but he was already looking for his next fight.

After retaining his WBC welterweight title, Garcia spotted WBA champion Teofimo Lopez at ringside and immediately called him into the ring.

Lopez appeared ready to accept the invitation, but security wouldn’t let him through.

That didn’t stop the two champions from shouting at each other across the barrier, with Garcia making it clear he wants a unification fight next.

Garcia holds the WBC belt and Lopez the WBA title, making a potential showdown much bigger than just their growing rivalry.

The face-off didn’t happen, but Garcia certainly got the message across.

articles.title: "KingRyan" becomes the most sought-after boxer after his exhibition against Benn
articles.standfirst: Dana White has no doubt: "He has knockout power, he's a handsome guy, he speaks well, and he doesn't duck anyone"
articles.summary: Dana White has no doubt: "He has knockout power, he's a handsome guy, he speaks well, and he doesn't duck anyone"
articles.body:
What we saw on Saturday night was a dazzling and devastating display by someone who may well become the next superstar of American boxing. Ryan García’s (26-2, 21 KOs) emphatic victory over Conor Benn (25-2, 14 KOs) significantly raised the Californian fighter’s profile in what was his first defense of the welterweight world title .

Although many question whether Benn was a top-level opponent , ‘KingRyan’ did what he had to do to become the boxer everyone wants to see, with all due respect to the Benavidezes, Inoue, or ‘Bam’ Rodríguez. García captivated the crowd and the event promoter Dana White (Zuffa Boxing) in just two rounds.

Zuffa’s evening went perfectly, starting with its promotion. The García-Benn fight received support on UFC broadcasts and social media, on WWE’s platforms, and at Fanatics Fest . The fighters, especially García, then fulfilled their role in the ring. Although Zuffa does not have Ryan’s rights, Dana White did not hesitate to heap praise on the boxer: “He has knockout power, he’s a handsome kid, he speaks well, and he doesn’t dodge anyone. This kid wants to fight everybody.”

The next target for García is to unify his title with the one held by Teófimo López in a headline bout that would take place on the weekend of Cinco de Mayo 2027. However, Turki Alalshikh, who promoted the fight between García and Benn together with White for Zuffa Boxing, has other plans, as he wants Terence Crawford to come out of retirement to face ‘KignRy’, according to Ring Magazine. The fight we definitely will not see would be a rematch against Gervonta Davis , as he insists he will not move up to welterweight and Ryan will no longer move down to lower divisions.

articles.title: Ryan Garcia confirms Gervonta Davis rematch talks but the terms have changed
articles.standfirst: Garcia confirms he won't repeat the compromises of 2023
articles.summary: Garcia confirms he won't repeat the compromises of 2023
articles.body:
Ryan Garcia has wanted another shot at Gervonta “Tank” Davis ever since their 2023 fight ended with him on the canvas. This time, though, he says he won't be the one making the major concessions.

Garcia confirmed that Davis and Premier Boxing Champions founder Al Haymon have contacted his team about a possible rematch, but he immediately set the parameters.

“I can confirm Gervonta and Al have contacted my team,” Garcia wrote on X. “147 or nothing.

“And I want him to get a tune up fight and be at his best when we fight,” Garcia added. “He has some stuff to handle but we forsure going to get it going on. LETS RUMBLE.”

That stance marks a significant reversal from their first meeting, when Garcia agreed to terms that heavily favored Davis .

First fight still shapes Garcia’s thinking

Garcia and Davis met in April 2023 at a 136-pound catchweight, with a rehydration clause preventing Garcia from weighing more than 146 pounds on fight day.

Davis won by seventh-round knockout after landing a body shot that Garcia couldn't recover from. Garcia has since insisted he wouldn't accept similar restrictions again.

“I need that if you want it,” he wrote while discussing a rematch at 147 pounds. “If not, there’s nothing to be said.”

He has also suggested 144 pounds could potentially be discussed, while ruling out a return to 140.

“There’s no way I’m going down to 140,” Garcia said in another exchange. “He got to come up to me sooner or later.”

Davis , responding through an account linked to him, appeared willing to move closer to Garcia ’s range.

“No lie for you, I’ll do 144…word, say it’s a bet!!” Davis wrote. “And I’ll get this sh*t I’m going through out the way! Just give the word!!”

Garcia has more leverage now

The biggest difference is where Garcia stands in 2026. After setbacks against Devin Haney and Rolando Romero , he rebuilt his position with a title win over Mario Barrios and then strengthened it further with a victory over Conor Benn .

Garcia now considers 147 pounds his division. Davis , by contrast, has spent most of his career at 130 and 135 pounds, with only limited experience above lightweight.

That makes the weight issue more than negotiating theater. A rematch is clearly back in play, but Garcia is no longer presenting himself as the fighter willing to bend just to make it happen.

Three years ago, he moved toward Davis . Now he expects Davis to move toward him.

articles.title: Jake Paul is accusing Ryan Garcia of costing Paramount tens of millions of dollars by challenging Terence Crawford
articles.standfirst: Jake Paul has taken aim at Ryan Garcia after the WBC welterweight champion reignited his feud with retired star Terence Crawford
articles.summary: Jake Paul has taken aim at Ryan Garcia after the WBC welterweight champion reignited his feud with retired star Terence Crawford
articles.body:
R yan Garcia 's victory over Conor Benn was supposed to be a major statement for both the fighter and Zuffa Boxing.

Instead, the aftermath has quickly become dominated by another storyline, with Jake Paul publicly criticizing Garcia over his decision to continue pursuing a potential fight with Terence Crawford .

Garcia stopped Benn in the second round at Las Vegas' T-Mobile Arena on September 12, retaining his WBC welterweight title in front of a sold-out crowd of 18,855.

Zuffa Boxing reported a live gate of more than $8 million for the event, while Paramount+ carried the card as part of its global streaming partnership with Zuffa Boxing.

But Garcia did not spend long celebrating. His ongoing verbal battle with Crawford intensified after the former undisputed champion responded to Garcia's repeated challenges.

Paul then entered the conversation with a now-deleted social-media post aimed directly at Garcia .

“Brother, you need to stop the bulls**it,” read the post from Paul . “ Crawford would take you down in two seconds and beat your a** in the streets. And so would I.”

Paul then made the financial accusation that has generated the most attention: “You just lost Paramount $10’s of millions. Only thing your the face of is that white power.”

The figure cited by Paul has not been independently established in the available public reporting, so his claim should be understood as an accusation rather than a confirmed measure of Paramount's financial loss.

Why Garcia's Crawford feud has become a business issue

The dispute between Garcia and Crawford did not suddenly appear after the Benn fight. Garcia had been questioning Crawford's career choices for months, particularly his decision to step away from professional boxing rather than continue taking on younger elite opponents.

Crawford , meanwhile, has repeatedly pushed back at Garcia's challenges. After Garcia defeated Benn, the argument became even more personal.

Speaking with Ariel Helwani, Garcia said, “He’s (Crawford) jealous of me. He knows that. He can’t deny that fact in him. He’s like, Damn, I don’t really like this f***er. Cool. Jealousy, motherf***er. I’ll beat the f*** out you. I’ll beat the jealous out of you.”

Crawford subsequently mocked Garcia for challenging him after his retirement and suggested Garcia should focus on active fighters. Garcia responded, “Okay, so let’s square up, bro, on or off the ring. I’m ready to handle this.”

That exchange is particularly relevant because Garcia's relationship with Paul has also deteriorated over time.

Paul and Garcia were once on friendly terms, but their relationship has become considerably more complicated. Paul also previously targeted Garcia as a potential opponent after a planned exhibition against Gervonta "Tank" Davis failed to materialize.

Garcia ultimately rejected an offer that was widely reported to have been worth around $20 million. Explaining his decision to Shannon Sharpe , Garcia said:

“I was offered Mario for a world title, and I said to myself, ‘If I’m always chasing money, I’m a real boxer, you know, and I have a world title on the line,'” Garcia told Shannon Sharpe . “And I just knew you chase money; nothing good comes out of it, right? I’ve done it before.”

“I’ve made this mistake before. Don’t chase the money…And then this little carrot came wiggling at me. I was like, nah, that doesn’t seem right. It’s temptation. I’m going to stick to what I know. And ultimately, I’m getting, you know, well, getting paid a lot of money for this fight. So, it’s like it worked out for me.”

That history gives Paul's criticism a personal dimension, but there is also an obvious promotional backdrop.

Conor Benn 's move to Zuffa Boxing was one of the promotion's biggest early statements. The Ring reported that Benn initially signed a one-fight agreement reportedly worth $15 million before agreeing to a five-fight extension through 2028.

Garcia's destruction of Benn therefore represented more than simply another win on his record. It was also the outcome of a heavily promoted event built around Zuffa's expanding presence in boxing and Paramount+'s investment in the sport.

Paramount officially described Garcia-Benn as a first-of-its-kind global Paramount+ event when the fight was announced, with the card available to subscribers at no additional cost in most markets.

Paul's argument appears to be that Garcia's continuing focus on Crawford could complicate the commercial possibilities that might otherwise surround Garcia's next fight. Whether that actually cost Paramount tens of millions, however, remains unproven.

There is another part of Garcia's history that continues to follow him. In 2024, the New York State Athletic Commission suspended him for one year after positive tests for the banned substance ostarine.

His victory over Devin Haney was subsequently changed to a no-contest, while Garcia forfeited his disclosed purse and received a $10,000 fine.

Garcia has since rebuilt his career and now holds the WBC welterweight championship after defeating Mario Barrios and successfully defending it against Benn. His latest victory was emphatic, with the referee stopping the contest 1:25 into the second round.

For now, Crawford does not appear interested in reversing his retirement for Garcia. After their latest exchange, Crawford told Garcia to focus on active names including Devin Haney, Keyshawn Davis, Shakur Stevenson, Richardson Hitchins and Teofimo Lopez .

Garcia, meanwhile, has plenty of options of his own. He has spoken about pursuing Teofimo Lopez and other major names, meaning the Crawford rivalry may remain a social-media story rather than becoming an immediate fight.

Paul's intervention has added another layer to the situation. What began as a fighter calling out a retired rival has now become a wider argument involving promoters, broadcasters, money and the commercial future of one of boxing's most marketable champions.
